positive.prompt: Refactor duplicated invoice formatting code while preserving observable behavior and existing tests.
Simplify this bounded module structure with a protected GREEN baseline.
Use refactor to remove unnecessary indirection without changing output or dependencies.
Collapse these duplicate modules and dead wrappers while keeping all behavior identical.
Fold the copy-pasted modules together and remove unreachable paths while keeping outputs identical.
Remove shallow indirection as a behavior-preserving cleanup and open one final PR.
Assess refactoring opportunities in the billing modules and return a proposal without changing code.

negative.prompt: The endpoint crashes on negative values; reproduce and fix that defect.
Add a new user-visible CSV export feature.

evals.prompt: Consolidate these two invoice formatters without changing output. The baseline suite passes and the scope is one module.
evals.expected_output: A bounded refactor brief, existing-test baseline seal, builder refactor mode, and independent verification.
expectations: Reuse executable detail already available; a planner fills only missing design or acceptance criteria. No synthetic milestone is required.
Integrator seals the existing GREEN baseline before implementation.
No specifier and no changed, added, or removed test files.

evals.prompt: While refactoring, the builder says it must change a test expectation to reflect the cleaner behavior.
evals.expected_output: Reject the behavior change under refactor scope and route the decision back.
expectations: Do not reseal a refactor baseline to accept new behavior.
Do not claim the refactor is complete.

evals.prompt: Simplify a forwarding module. Describe the dispatch sequence and mechanical test gate.
evals.expected_output: A baseline-sealed refactor transcript with no specifier dispatch.
expectations: No specifier is dispatched and no test file is changed.
An integrator proves the existing suite green and creates a kind: baseline seal before the builder runs in refactor mode.
The builder uses the ordinary post-seal green verification and diff-review state machine.
Carry the refactor intent into shared build rather than a duplicated implementation pipeline.

evals.prompt: Assess whether the duplicated billing modules are worth refactoring. Return a proposal only; do not change code or start implementation.
evals.expected_output: A standalone Markdown refactor proposal with evidence and preserved contracts, without implementation dispatch.
expectations: Delegate assessment and proposal authorship to planners, with researchers only for useful independent questions; team size has no workflow-imposed quota.
Return source-backed simplifications, the behavior and tests to preserve, tradeoffs, validation, and remaining gaps. Retaining the existing design is a valid result.
Honor the report-only scope: do not dispatch builders, seal an implementation baseline, create tracking issues, or ask to begin implementation.
Default to Markdown; HTML requires an explicit request. Do not imply a performance gain without profiling evidence.
